# Making the Graph Tools Actionable

> ⚠️ **Recorded after the fact, 2026-08-07.** These three fixes shipped during device testing with no spec entry at all. That is a traceability failure of mine, not a process gap — the rule was already written down. Logged here so the reasoning survives the session that produced it.
Three defects reported from the device, all the same shape: **a tool named a problem the operator could not reach.**
## 1. Connect the Graph reported counts with no records
Operator: *"It tells me that 90 performer traits are on videos but doesn't give me a list... I can't find either of these in the videos. How do I fix the error if it don't take me to the problems?"*
The screen showed bare counts. The codebase already states the rule it was breaking — the batch runs say *"a tally you cannot act on is a dead end"* — and this screen broke it four times over.
Worse, two of the three blockers **had their lists already** and discarded them at the display layer. The third never captured one: `attributeTagsOnVideos` was an `Int`, so `connectTagEdges` incremented a counter and threw away which tag and which video.
**Fixed:**
- `TagConnectPlan.attributeTagsOnVideos` is now `[String: Int]` — keyed by tag, valued by video count. The old total survives as `attributeTagAssociations`.
- Every blocker lists its records, capped at 12 with *"and N more"* said out loud, and **each row is a link** that filters the library to that name or tag.
- ⚠️ Filtering by a performer name works even with no profile, because the grid matches the `actor:` string — which is exactly the population this blocker is about.
## 2. 🚨 The actor batch run was blind to the actors that needed it
Operator: *"When I go to the actor matching bulk utility it skips 100% of my actors. I've got over a hundred in the not-yet-checked status when I filter on that."*
Both statements were true simultaneously. **Nothing creates an actor profile row when a video match adds a cast member**, so those actors exist only as `actor:Name` strings. The gallery builds its list from the strings; the batch run iterated `fetchAllEntityProfiles()`.
So they were not skipped — they were **invisible**. The run examined only the already-matched profiles and truthfully reported "100% skipped" about a list that excluded everyone who mattered. Same root cause as Connect the Graph's *"190 names have no profile"*: one bug, two symptoms, reported days apart.
**Fixed:** the run now works from every actor **name** in the library, profile rows unioned with the names on videos.
🚨 **With a guard that is a decision, not a detail.** A name with no profile becomes a *person* only when the source confirms one. A `noMatch` or `ambiguous` verdict against a rowless name writes **nothing** — recording it would mint a profile for a name a filename may have guessed, which the Epic forbids (D3), and would then let Connect the Graph wire credits to a person nobody has verified.
⚠️ **Known cost:** unmatched names stay rowless, so every re-run examines them again and spends the requests. That is the right trade against inventing people, but it is a real cost and worth revisiting if the same names are re-searched indefinitely.
## 3. Studio spelling collisions routed to a tool that could not fix them
Operator, with a screenshot of ten collisions: *"Studios spelled two ways asks to use the tag spelling fix, not a studio fix."*
Correct, and worse than a mislabelled link. `TagCaseAudit` reads `Asset.actions`, which filters to `tag:` values — **a ****`studio:`**** value is never in the set it examines.** Repair Tag Spelling could not have fixed a single one. The routing was chosen by name similarity rather than by checking what the tool operates on.
**Fixed:** `StudioFix.repairTagSpelling` becomes `repairStudioSpelling`, and a real `StudioSpellingCleanupView` exists. Folded through `StudioResolution.identity` so spacing collisions are caught — nine of the operator's ten differ only by spacing, which a case-only fold would miss entirely. Most-used spelling wins; **on a tie the spaced form wins**, because a run-together name is what a source produces when it drops the spaces and the spaced one is what a person wrote.
A test now asserts `TagCaseAudit.tagCounts` returns empty for a library of studio collisions while the studio audit finds them — so the two can never be confused again.
## The pattern worth keeping
All three were **reported by using the app**, and none would have been found by reading code — two of them I had already reasoned about and got wrong. The recurring shape is a tool that is *correct about its own inputs* while being useless about the operator's question:
- a count computed correctly over the wrong set,
- a list computed and discarded,
- a route chosen by name rather than by capability.
⭐ **A tool that reports a problem must be able to reach it.** Worth treating as a design rule rather than three separate bugs.
## Verification
LibraryCore 1,146 tests, 0 failures. macOS and iOS build. D9 clean. Committed in `70278b0`.
⚠️ None of this is device-verified beyond the operator's original reports — the fixes were built after each report and have not been confirmed in use.
